memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Maya chose the lower total-cost Friday itinerary after confirming that both finalists met the trip's nonstop and Wi-Fi requirements; she did not allow the cheaper airfare alone to outweigh the added hotel cost or the required transfer margin.

messages.content: I need to sort out Denver for the client workshop. It runs Wednesday through Friday, ending at 2:00 Friday downtown. I can leave Minneapolis Tuesday after 4:30, and the airfare cap is $650. Can you compare Friday evening with Saturday morning coming back?
What dates are the workshop, and do you need nonstop service or any onboard feature such as Wi-Fi?
The workshop is May 27 through May 29, so outbound Tuesday May 26. Nonstop and Wi-Fi are required. Wednesday starts at 8:00 a.m., so I don't want to arrive that morning.

I found three nonstop economy combinations with Wi-Fi under the cap. The strongest outbound for all of them leaves MSP Tuesday at 5:35 p.m. and reaches DEN at 6:42 p.m. The alternatives leaving after 7:00 p.m. arrive around 8:30 or later, which still works but leaves less recovery time before the workshop. For the return, the useful choices are Friday at 5:20 p.m. for a $438 round trip, Friday at 7:05 p.m. for $472, or Saturday at 8:10 a.m. for $421.
Is 5:20 actually reasonable from downtown after a 2:00 finish, or does it only work on paper?

It is possible but tight. Allowing about 10 minutes to wrap up and leave, the train typically puts you at DEN around 3:05–3:20; a car can vary more with Friday traffic. That leaves roughly two hours before departure, but only about 75–90 minutes before boarding. A late workshop finish, a delayed train, or a bag-check line would erode the margin quickly.
I will have a checked demo case, and I can't leave the workshop early. Rule out 5:20. How does the 7:05 compare with staying Friday night?

The 7:05 p.m. Friday flight gives you a much healthier transfer: leaving downtown around 2:20–2:30 should get you to the terminal about 3:20–3:45, with ample time to check the case. It arrives MSP at 10:02 p.m. The Saturday 8:10 a.m. flight arrives at 11:04 a.m. and costs $51 less, but it adds a hotel night and requires leaving downtown around 5:30 a.m.
The project will cover Friday night if needed, but I'd prefer not to add it without a good reason. Are there any later Friday nonstops?

There is an 8:35 p.m. nonstop arriving MSP at 11:31 p.m. for $519 round trip. It provides the easiest Friday margin, though it is $47 more than the 7:05 and gets you home about ninety minutes later. All three remaining combinations include Wi-Fi and stay below the $650 airfare limit.
Then the real choices are 7:05 Friday or 8:10 Saturday. Does the cheaper Saturday fare still save anything once the hotel is included?

No. The fare saves $51, but even a modest downtown Friday-night hotel near $160 before tax makes the Saturday plan at least about $120 more expensive overall. Saturday is useful only if the workshop may run substantially late or you want to avoid traveling Friday evening.
The end time is firm. Since both choices meet the nonstop and Wi-Fi requirements, take the lower total-cost option rather than paying for an extra night.

That makes the Friday 7:05 p.m. return the better choice: MSP to DEN Tuesday May 26, 5:35–6:42 p.m.; DEN to MSP Friday May 29, 7:05–10:02 p.m.; nonstop economy with Wi-Fi, $472 round trip. The checked demo case may add a bag fee depending on the fare terms.
Good. Keep one backup in case that return jumps in price, but don't book either one yet.

Primary itinerary: Tuesday 5:35 p.m. MSP–DEN and Friday 7:05 p.m. DEN–MSP, nonstop with Wi-Fi, currently $472 round trip. Backup: the same Tuesday outbound with the Saturday 8:10 a.m.–11:04 a.m. nonstop return, currently $421, plus a Friday hotel night and early airport transfer. The Friday 5:20 option is excluded because the checked case and fixed 2:00 p.m. workshop finish leave too little margin. Nothing has been booked or charged.
